conversation: Good to see everyone. My family taught me that looking after the lake means looking after the village. With 100 tons in it now, I suggest we each catch 10 tons this month. That leaves 50 to double back to 100, giving each of us $10,000 a month if we stick to it. We can review everyone’s catches together each month and adjust if the stock falls short. Are you all willing to agree to that? John, what do you think?

I’m in, Luke—10 tons each gives us a steady living without running down the lake our families depend on. Let’s agree that any increase needs everyone’s approval, and if the lake starts a month below 100 tons, we lower our catches to leave at least half the stock to reproduce. John, can you commit to that too?

Count me in for 10 tons. My family taught me not to take tomorrow’s catch today, and this gives all five families a steady income. If the stock drops below 100, let’s split no more than half of what’s there equally and review how to rebuild it. Kate, Emma—are you both comfortable with that agreement?

I’m comfortable with that—count me in for 10 tons. This lake has supported my family for generations, and I want it to keep supporting all our families. Let’s check the stock together before each month’s catch and keep a shared record so we all know where we stand. Emma, does that work for you?

That works for me—I'll take 10 tons this month and stick to our agreed limits. I learned to fish here with my family, and I want the village’s children to have that same chance. With all five of us agreed, let’s record the catches and meet again at month’s end. If anyone needs extra income, let’s talk before taking extra fish.
